s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with rapid progression of motor and autonomic dysfunction
key_facts: 42-year-old man with 30 pack-years of smoking
Cannabis use, alcohol dependence, and use of herbal products
3-day history of acute symptoms
Marked paraparesis of the lower limbs (muscle strength 2/5)
Normal sensory function, including proprioception, light touch, and vibration
Normal cranial nerve and upper limb examinations
Febrile and respiratory distress requiring intubation and sedation
Clear cerebrospinal fluid without albuminocytologic dissociation
Abnormal blood tests, including anemia, leukocytosis, and elevated liver enzymes
Multiple bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions on brain MRI
Diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar cord on spinal MRI

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of motor and autonomic dysfunction, multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions on brain MRI, and diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the spinal cord

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of neurological symptoms, including paraparesis and hyperreflexia, with involvement of the spinal cord and brainstem

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions on brain MRI, and diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the spinal cord, although the rapid progression is atypical

shortlist.label: Acute Transverse Myelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of paraparesis and hyperreflexia, with diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the spinal cord

shortlist.label: Devic's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Optic neuritis and myelitis, with rapid progression of neurological symptoms, although the absence of optic neuritis in the case description makes this less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including acute onset of neurological deficits, febrile illness, and respiratory distress, along with the presence of multiple bilateral symmetrical lesions on brain MRI and diffuse T2 hyperintensities on spinal MRI, are consistent with Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM). The lack of albuminocytologic dissociation in the cerebrospinal fluid also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: The patient's brain MRI shows multiple bilateral symmetrical lesions, which is not typical for Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder, and the absence of optic neuritis also makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings are more consistent with a monophasic illness, such as ADEM, rather than the relapsing-remitting course typical of Multiple Sclerosis.

rejected.label: Acute Transverse Myelitis
rejected.why: While the patient has spinal cord involvement, the presence of brain lesions and the overall clinical presentation are more consistent with ADEM than with Acute Transverse Myelitis.

rejected.label: Devic's Disease
rejected.why: Devic's Disease is a form of Neuromyelitis Optica, and the patient's brain MRI and clinical presentation do not support this diagnosis.
